questions.stem: What is « une famille nombreuse »?
options: a large family with many children
a family with famous members
a family living in a big house
a family spread over many countries
questions.explanation: « Nombreux » means numerous. In France, a family with three or more children is officially « une famille nombreuse ».

questions.stem: What is « une famille monoparentale »?
options: a family with one child
a family with two mothers
a family run by grandparents
a single-parent family
questions.explanation: « Mono- » means one, so one parent raises the children. A family with one child has « un enfant unique ».

questions.stem: « Mes parents ne sont pas mariés, ils sont pacsés. » What does « pacsés » mean?
options: living in different houses
joined by a civil partnership
separated but still good friends
engaged to be married soon
questions.explanation: The PACS (pacte civil de solidarité), created in 1999, is a legal partnership open to any two adults, an alternative to marriage that many French couples choose.

questions.stem: « Je suis l'aîné de trois enfants. » What does the speaker say?
options: He is the youngest of three children
He is the middle child of three
He has three older siblings
He is the eldest of three children
questions.explanation: « L'aîné(e) » is the eldest. The youngest is « le cadet » or « la cadette », or « le benjamin » for the very youngest.

questions.stem: What are « les tâches ménagères »?
options: household chores
school assignments
shopping errands
garden plants
questions.explanation: « Les tâches ménagères » are jobs around the house such as cleaning, cooking and washing.

questions.stem: « Chez nous, mon père fait la cuisine et ma mère s'occupe du jardin : on ne suit pas les clichés. » What is the speaker's point?
options: Her family always eats meals from the garden
Her family does not follow gender stereotypes
Her family follows traditional roles closely
Her parents both refuse to do any housework
questions.explanation: « Les clichés » here are stereotypes about who does what at home. The father cooks and the mother gardens, against the traditional pattern.

questions.stem: What is « un père au foyer »?
options: a father who lives in a hostel
a stay-at-home dad
a father who works abroad
a foster father
questions.explanation: « Au foyer » means at home, so he looks after the home and children instead of working outside. « Une mère au foyer » is the traditional counterpart.

questions.stem: « Chez nous, on partage les tâches à parts égales. » What does it mean?
options: We share our things with others
We take turns paying the bills
We do the chores at the same time
We share the chores equally
questions.explanation: « À parts égales » means in equal shares. The sentence describes a fair division of housework.

questions.stem: « Mes parents interdisent les téléphones à table : le dîner, c'est le moment de discuter. » What does this show about family life?
options: Phones are allowed at the table only at dinner
The parents eat dinner without the children
Meals are kept as time for talking together
The family never talks during dinner
questions.explanation: « Interdire » means to ban. The rule protects the evening meal as family conversation time.

questions.stem: « Le dimanche, toute la famille se réunit chez mes grands-parents. » What happens on Sundays?
options: The family holds a meeting about the grandparents
The grandparents go out without the family
The whole family gathers at the grandparents' home
The grandparents visit each family in turn
questions.explanation: « Se réunir » means to get together, and « chez mes grands-parents » means at their home. Sunday lunch with the extended family is a common French tradition.

questions.stem: « Mamie garde mes petits cousins le mercredi. » What does Grandma do?
options: She stays with my cousins every week
She visits my small cousins on weekends
She minds my young cousins on Wednesdays
She keeps my cousins' presents on Wednesdays
questions.explanation: « Garder des enfants » means to look after them. Grandparents often mind children on Wednesdays, when many French primary schools have no classes.

questions.stem: « Je ne vois mes cousins qu'aux fêtes de fin d'année, mais on s'appelle en visio chaque semaine. » How does the speaker stay close to them?
options: letters at the end of each year, as they never meet
phone calls only at Christmas and New Year
weekly video calls, as they meet only at the holidays
weekly visits, as they live in the same street
questions.explanation: « Ne… que » means only: she sees them only at the end-of-year holidays. « En visio » is short for « en visioconférence », a video call.

questions.stem: « Mon beau-père est très sympa. » Who could « mon beau-père » be?
options: my handsome father or my grandfather
my godfather or my uncle
my older brother or my cousin
my stepfather or my father-in-law
questions.explanation: « Beau- » in family words marks a relation by marriage: « beau-père » is a stepfather or a father-in-law. A godfather is « un parrain ».

questions.stem: What are « le parrain » and « la marraine » of a child?
options: the uncle and the aunt
the godfather and the godmother
the grandfather and the grandmother
the stepfather and the stepmother
questions.explanation: A godparent is chosen at a child's birth or baptism and often keeps a special bond with the child. Grandparents are « le grand-père » and « la grand-mère ».

questions.stem: « Elle est ma meilleure amie depuis la maternelle. » Since when have they been friends?
options: since high school
since last summer
since university
since preschool
questions.explanation: « La maternelle » is the French nursery or preschool, from about age three. « Depuis » plus the present shows the friendship is still going.

questions.stem: « On s'est brouillés à cause d'une rumeur. » What happened?
options: They started a rumour together
They met because of a rumour
They fell out because of a rumour
They made up after hearing a rumour
questions.explanation: « Se brouiller » means to fall out. « Se réconcilier » is to make up, and « à cause de » gives a negative cause.

questions.stem: « On s'est perdus de vue après le collège. » What does it mean?
options: We stopped seeing well after collège
We became close after collège
We lost touch after collège
We got lost on the way to collège
questions.explanation: « Se perdre de vue » means to lose touch with each other. Nothing is literally lost.

questions.stem: « Je peux toujours compter sur elle. » What does it mean?
options: I can always beat her
I can always count on her
I can always count her money
I always tell her my secrets
questions.explanation: « Compter sur quelqu'un » means to rely on someone. It is a key phrase for describing what makes a good friend.

questions.stem: « Un vrai ami, c'est quelqu'un qui te dit la vérité, même quand ça fait mal. » What does the writer value?
options: kindness that avoids hurting you
loyalty that hides the truth
fun more than serious talk
honesty, even when it hurts
questions.explanation: « Même quand ça fait mal » means even when it hurts, so honesty matters more than comfort.

questions.stem: What is « un groupe de discussion » on a phone?
options: a support line
a group chat
a phone plan
a debating team
questions.explanation: Young people connect through « des groupes de discussion » on messaging apps, sharing news and plans.

questions.stem: « Les réseaux sociaux permettent de garder le contact, mais rien ne remplace un vrai moment ensemble. » What is the writer's view?
options: Meeting in person is less useful than social media
Social media keep contact, but meeting up is better
Social media have replaced spending time together
Social media make it harder to stay in contact
questions.explanation: « Rien ne remplace » means nothing replaces. The writer concedes a benefit of social media, then values time together more.

questions.stem: « Il est jaloux de mon amitié avec Léa. » How does he feel?
options: proud
relieved
grateful
jealous
questions.explanation: « Jaloux » (feminine « jalouse ») means jealous. Jealousy is one of the challenges of friendship that texts often explore.

questions.stem: « Quand on déménage, il faut tout recommencer : nouvelle école, nouveaux amis. » What challenge is described?
options: Changing schools always means moving to a new house in town
New friends make it hard to stay at the same school
Moving house is easy when you change schools
Moving house means starting over at school and with friends
questions.explanation: « Déménager » means to move house, and « tout recommencer » to start everything again. Making new friends is part of the challenge.

questions.stem: In France, what is « le collège »?
options: a university college for undergraduates
a private boarding school for older students
the final two years of secondary school
lower secondary school, for about ages 11 to 15
questions.explanation: French students go from primary school to « le collège » (four years) and then to « le lycée ». University is « l'université » or « la fac ».

questions.stem: Which class is the first year of the French lycée?
options: la sixième
la terminale
la troisième
la seconde
questions.explanation: The lycée runs « seconde », « première », then « terminale ». « La sixième » is the first year of collège and « la troisième » the last.

questions.stem: French school years count down. Which statement is correct?
options: La sixième begins collège and la troisième ends it
La troisième begins collège and la sixième ends it
La sixième and la troisième are both lycée years
La sixième and la troisième are both primary years
questions.explanation: Collège runs sixième, cinquième, quatrième, troisième, so the numbers fall as students move up. The brevet exam comes at the end of troisième.

questions.stem: What is « le brevet »?
options: a certificate for learning to swim at school
a report card sent home each term
the national exam at the end of collège
the school-leaving exam at the end of lycée
questions.explanation: « Le diplôme national du brevet » is taken at about 15, at the end of troisième. The bac comes at the end of lycée.

questions.stem: « J'ai eu 15 sur 20 en maths. » What does the student say?
options: She got 15 of the maths questions wrong
She studied maths for 15 hours
She failed her maths test badly
She got a good mark of 15 out of 20
questions.explanation: French marks are usually out of 20, and 15 is a good result. Ten is the usual pass mark.

questions.stem: What does « redoubler » mean at school?
options: to repeat a year
to skip a year
to double your marks
to change schools
questions.explanation: « Redoubler » is to repeat a school year after poor results. It is less common in France than it once was.

questions.stem: « Le midi, je mange à la cantine. » Where does the student eat lunch?
options: at home with her family
at a café in town
in the classroom
in the school canteen
questions.explanation: « La cantine » serves hot meals at school, usually a starter, main course and dessert. Many French students eat there every day.

questions.stem: « En France, la plupart des élèves ne portent pas d'uniforme, alors qu'en Australie, c'est presque toujours obligatoire. » What contrast is drawn?
options: French students wear uniforms more often than Australians
Uniforms are banned in both France and Australia
Australian students choose freely whether to wear one
Most French students wear no uniform; most Australians do
questions.explanation: « Alors que » means whereas, and sets the two countries side by side. « La plupart » means most.

questions.stem: In France, what is « la rentrée »?
options: the end of the school year in July
the return home after school each day
the entrance exam for a lycée
the start of the school year in September
questions.explanation: « La rentrée » is the return to school after the long summer break, in early September, unlike Australia's late January or early February start.

questions.stem: « Les journées sont longues : de 8 h à 17 h, avec une pause d'une heure et demie à midi. » What does the student say about her school day?
options: It is long, with a lunch break of an hour and a half
It is short, ending at lunchtime every single day
It starts at 8 pm and ends at 5 am
It has no lunch break at all
questions.explanation: « De 8 h à 17 h » is 8 am to 5 pm, and « une heure et demie » is an hour and a half. Long days and a long lunch break are common in French schools.

questions.stem: What is « le bulletin scolaire »?
options: a school newsletter
a school bus
a school notice board
a school report
questions.explanation: « Le bulletin » lists a student's marks and teachers' comments each term. A newsletter is « la lettre d'information ».

questions.stem: « J'ai la pression : mes parents veulent que j'aie de bonnes notes pour entrer dans un bon lycée. » What challenge does the student face?
options: pressure from her parents to get good marks
pressure from her friends to skip some classes
a lack of interest in going to lycée
a teacher who gives very low marks
questions.explanation: « Avoir la pression » means to feel under pressure, and « veulent que j'aie » (subjunctive) shows what the parents want.

questions.stem: In a French collège or lycée, who is « le CPE »?
options: the nurse who looks after sick students
the staff member in charge of student life and discipline
the principal who runs the whole school and its budget
the teacher who gives careers advice
questions.explanation: « Le conseiller principal d'éducation » oversees attendance, behaviour and student welfare outside lessons, with the « surveillants ». The principal of a lycée is « le proviseur ».
